To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ribulose  1,5- bisphosphate carboxy-lase/oxygenase is synthesized as a larger precursor in the cytoplasm and is imported into the stroma of the chloroplast in an ATP- and energy-dependent process, where it is processed to its mature size and assembled with the other subunit to form the holoenzyme.
(i) the chloroplast synthesises only a limited number (about 20) of its own proteins, the rest being made by the cytosol.

the large subunits of RUBISCO, a chloroplast enzyme, are synthesized by the chloroplast and that the large subunit precursor is synthesized in the cytosolic fraction of the chloroplast, transported across the chloroplast envelope membranes, and assembled with the small subunit in the chloroplast.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (a) the identification of the transport signals and the mechanism of transport of the stromal enzymes, (b) the identification of transport signals and the transport mechanism of the thylakoid membrane proteins, and (c) the mechanism of assembly of the stromal enzyme ribulose 5-phosphate carboxyl-ase (Rubisco) in the chloroplast.
the mechanism of intracellular transfer of proteins and with the mechanism of assembly of the chloroplast enzyme ribulose 15-bisphosphate (RuBP) carboxylase (2).
understanding the mechanisms of protein synthesis, transport, folding, and assembly of proteins in chloroplasts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanism of transport of proteins across membranes is still not understood and is the subject of active investigation.
the chloroplast is capable of synthesizing a limited number of polypeptides and that the remainder are synthesized in the cytosolic compartment and transported into the chloroplast.
the chloroplasts of the plant kingdom contain a large number of proteins, which are not synthesized by them but are synthesized by cytosol and are transported into chloroplasts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ribosomes are not attached to the chloroplast envelope membrane, and the polypeptides synthesized in the cytoplasm are translocated through the membrane by an energy-dependent process.
the chloroplast envelope membranes contain a protein transport system that is specific for chloroplast proteins.
we have shown that ribulose-1,5-bi-sphosphate carboxy-lase is synthesized in the cytosolic fraction of the cell and is transported into the chloroplast.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chloroplast is a very dynamic organelle.
the chloroplast has the capacity to synthesize and transport proteins, but it does not do so for all proteins that it needs.
the chloroplast has the capacity to import proteins and that this process is not limited by a shortage of energy or by the presence of a permeability barrier at the outer envelope.
